title: One Of The Worst Classroom Management Strategies I've Ever Seen trategies-ive-ever-seen/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: After observing a training on a popular token-economy program, Linsin revisits his long-standing criticism of rewarding students for expected behavior, arguing such systems encourage cheating, weaken relationships, and snuff out intrinsic motivation. His sharpest criticism, though, targets a specific tactic demonstrated at the training called "caught being good," in which a misbehaving student is ignored while nearby well-behaved students are praised effusively, with the hope that the offender will be enticed by the attention. Linsin calls this approach dishonest, cruel, and demeaning, arguing it uses well-behaved students as pawns and offers the misbehaving student no genuine feedback for improvement. As an alternative, he lays out a series of direct principles: establish and defend clear behavioral boundaries, hold students accountable fairly and respectfully, praise only what is genuinely praiseworthy, and treat every student with honesty and dignity. The piece closes by arguing that only truth-based praise and consequences will carry real meaning and prepare students for life beyond the classroom.
points: Token economies encourage cheating and stealing, weaken the student-teacher relationship, and undermine intrinsic motivation.
The "caught being good" tactic — praising well-behaved neighbors while ignoring a misbehaving student — is dishonest and uses other students as pawns.
This tactic offers the misbehaving student no genuine feedback they can use to actually improve their behavior.
The alternative is to establish clear behavioral boundaries, defend them consistently, and hold students accountable fairly and respectfully.
Praise should be reserved for what is genuinely praiseworthy — concrete evidence of real progress or effort — so it carries lasting meaning.
quotes: I won't mention the program by name, but at its core, it's a token economy, whereby students are rewarded in exchange for 'good' (i.e. expected) behavior.
Worst of all, though, token economies snuff out intrinsic motivation.
In other words, you would ignore the misbehaving student, but effusively inform those in proximity how wonderful they are for doing what they're supposed to do.
It’s also cruel and demeaning and, in this case, uses well-behaved students as pawns to elicit compliant behavior from the misbehaving student.
That this method is endorsed, taught, and even promoted in school districts around the country is tragic and shameful.
Praise only what is praiseworthy. Look for legitimate improvement, new learning, or greater effort than they’ve given before, and then let them know you notice.

This way, your words of praise will mean something to them, firing their intrinsic motivational engines deep within their heart. They’ll know that if you said it, it must be true. And the truth will set them free.
